title: Advancing safety through connected and autonomous vehicles: a meta-analysis of market penetration and safety improvement rates from 2015 to 2024
short_title: CAV market penetration and safety meta-analysis
authors: Taheri, A., Yang, J., Müller, S., Milakis, D., et al.
methods: Cochran's Q, I-squared, and tau-squared heterogeneity assessment
comparison of logarithmic, linear, exponential, and power fits
sir_definition: SIR = ((CN0 - CNx) / CN0) x 100%, where CN0 is the conflict count in the zero-CAV baseline and CNx is the conflict count at a selected CAV market penetration rate.

reported_best_fit.interpretation: The paper reports that the power form fits the refined MPR-SIR relationship better than the tested linear and exponential alternatives.

reconstructed_display_curve.status: Dashboard display guide reconstructed from the nine rounded, sensitivity-adjusted values published in the article; it is not presented as the paper's exact printed coefficient equation.

consistent_with_web_app: Both bodies of work use simulation-derived traffic conflicts and surrogate safety measures rather than observed crash outcomes.
TTC-based evidence is central to both the literature synthesis and the Berlin SUMO analysis.
Both examine how automated-vehicle market penetration relates to safety outcomes in mixed traffic.
Both require sensitivity-aware and context-bounded interpretation rather than universal causal claims.
comparison_boundaries: The meta-analysis pools heterogeneous studies, networks, technologies, and surrogate measures; the web app analyzes one prepared Berlin SUMO study design.
Published SIR values are relative reductions from each study's zero-CAV baseline; dashboard conflict counts and severe-conflict shares are not automatically SIR values.
The meta-analysis benchmark must not be used to overwrite, validate, or numerically blend with the local simulation outputs.
Neither source alone establishes observed crash reduction or a causal effect for an untested deployment.
agent_rules: Identify the source as a published literature benchmark before quoting an MPR-SIR value.
Cite the DOI for every substantive benchmark answer.
Keep literature evidence separate from Berlin dashboard evidence.
Use only the nine published adjusted MPR-SIR points for exact benchmark values.
Describe the reconstructed curve as an approximate display guide, not the exact published equation.

chunks.heading: Literature benchmark - scope and method
chunks.text: The open-access study synthesizes 49 studies and reports 354 effect sizes from 2015-2024. It uses PRISMA/PICO selection, inverse-variance weighting, a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, heterogeneity assessment, publication-bias tests, trim-and-fill correction, and focused sensitivity analysis.

chunks.heading: Literature benchmark - refined MPR-SIR results
chunks.text: The sensitivity-adjusted Safety Improvement Rate values are 2.8%, 4.9%, 8.0%, 9.4%, 17.7%, 21.4%, 28.5%, 33.8%, and 39.4% at CAV market penetration rates of 10% through 90% in ten-point increments. The paper reports a power model as the best fit with R-squared 0.9928.

chunks.heading: Literature benchmark - surrogate safety measures
chunks.text: TTC-family measures account for 64% of the included analyses, PET for 15%, and other surrogate measures for 21%. This supports the relevance of TTC-based dashboard interpretation while also showing that a single surrogate measure does not capture every safety dimension.

chunks.heading: Literature benchmark - interpretation boundary
chunks.text: The benchmark aggregates heterogeneous simulation contexts and should be treated as indicative rather than definitive. It is not a direct validation of the Berlin SUMO scenarios, and its SIR values must not be substituted for local conflict counts, severe-conflict shares, or crash outcomes.
